subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom yielding glob walker and inter-handler bootstrap scheduling as the permanent compatibility-preserving fix for bootstrap event-loop stalls?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound and well proven, but only an owner can decide whether maintaining Node-glob parity in custom runtime code and allowing event-loop interleaving between bootstrap handlers is preferable to retaining the current scheduling behavior.

options.title: Accept after exact-head validation
options.body: Approve the compatibility-preserving walker and hook scheduling once the branch is rebased and all agent-runtime, SDK-surface, and parity checks pass on the exact head.

options.title: Require live channel-load proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live embedded run with active channel or WebSocket traffic confirms message delivery and session context remain stable during a large bootstrap scan.

options.title: Keep native glob behavior
options.body: Decline the custom walker and pursue a narrower upstream, worker-isolation, or different scheduling approach despite the current benchmarked improvement.

recommendation.title: Accept after exact-head validation
recommendation.body: Approve the compatibility-preserving walker and hook scheduling once the branch is rebased and all agent-runtime, SDK-surface, and parity checks pass on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail connects this person to the bootstrap cache, workspace loader, and adjacent embedded-run ownership boundary.
